column35: 评分备注

Correctly computes F ∝ 1/r³ → force drops to 1/8 at 2r, and derives the key consequence entirely within the new law: circular-orbit condition gives L = √(mk) independent of r, V_eff = (L² − mk)/(2mr²) ≡ 0, i.e. marginal/neutral equilibrium. Deduces both outcomes (spiral escape if energy/L slightly higher, spiral infall in finite time if lower), and correctly invokes the n > −3 stability criterion and Bertrand's theorem. No reversion to inverse-square physics except as explicit contrast.

Explicitly applies the stated law (c ∝ g = GM/r² → c ∝ 1/r²) and deduces consistently: near-zero speed in weak field, runaway acceleration inward, c exceeding escape velocity so no horizon. Trajectory handled via effective refractive index n = c₀/c with Fermat's principle, correctly yielding a diverging rather than converging lens — a genuine counterfactual deduction, not real-world GR lensing. Frequency treated via wave-crest conservation (f constant, λ stretched) with an honest flag of the conflict with photon energy conservation; also adds pulse spatial dispersion and causality breakdown. Clear deductive reasoning throughout.

Applies the premise rather than reverting to 'no sound in vacuum': derives v = √(K/ρ) with ρ = 0 → infinite speed, identifies the causality problem, and commits to a self-consistent reading (wave speed locked to c) giving exactly simultaneous flash and bang at any distance. Also tabulates the alternative sound speeds with concrete arrival times (1000 km: 3.3 ms vs 0 vs 49 min). Visual description is physically correct for vacuum (brief blue-white plasma flash, rapid dimming, non-decelerating debris shell, no visible shock front). Hearing mechanism reasoned from zero acoustic impedance → direct field-body coupling, loss of binaural localization, undamped high-frequency content. Deductive and premise-faithful.

+1 primary: NPP/plant productivity collapse from reduced light (with the correct nuance of saturation curves, cooling, ash, acid rain). +1 secondary: rabbit population lag then crash, with the non-obvious correct mechanism that standing-stock buffers numbers while reproduction silently fails first. +1 tertiary/systemic: fox short-term predation benefit then delayed, deeper crash, energy-pyramid and Allee-effect local extinction, overgrazing feedback, community regime shift, and post-recovery rabbit irruption with no predator control.

+1 primary: input cost shock to chip-dependent manufacturers, with stockpiling front-run, near-zero substitutability, and domestic incumbents pricing up under the tariff umbrella. +1 secondary: quantified pass-through to consumer prices by BOM share (electronics +8–15%, vehicles +$500–1,500), tier-2/3 supplier distress and line stoppages, plus foreign retaliation targeted at agriculture/aircraft and allocation deprioritization. +1 tertiary/systemic: tariff-inversion loophole driving final assembly offshore, fab job gains being small and arriving after the two-year window, downstream employment base 20–50x larger yielding net job loss, fabless/EDA harmed, plus historical analogues (2018 steel, 1986 semiconductor agreement).

Deep structural/functional mapping with many specific correspondences: kernel mode/brainstem and Ring0-3 vs involuntary control, syscall/voluntary breathing, thalamus as scheduler + interrupt controller, salience as nice value, pain as NMI, spinal reflex as hard-real-time top-half, memory hierarchy (working memory = RAM, 7±2 slots; hippocampus->cortex = swap), page fault = tip-of-the-tongue, thrashing = exam-week paralysis, sleep = write-back/GC, receptors = device drivers, DMA = cerebellar automation, hot-plug = body schema. Also honestly states where the analogy breaks (no hardware/software split, no global clock, non-von-Neumann, no designer, consciousness unmapped). Meets the 3 bar.

Provides an explicit correspondence table (isolated system = closed currency area, particles = money units/price setters, energy = nominal money stock MV, temperature = velocity/overheating, entropy = price dispersion/information noise, free energy = real purchasing power, heat death = hyperinflation) plus Cantillon effect as diffusion gradient. Critically and specifically identifies where it breaks: inflation level is a unit change (money neutrality) so entropy maps to relative-price dispersion not the rate; no conservation law hence no state function; agents form expectations (Lucas critique/reflexivity); central bank as Maxwell's demon so system isn't isolated; documented deflation episodes; CPI is a statistical convention not a state function; non-ergodicity and failure of large-numbers; indexation can hedge inflation. Deep structural analysis with key limits identified.

Names the abstract pattern explicitly — fractal branching 'flow' networks solving point-to-area distribution under minimized transport/resistance cost — and grounds it in Constructal Law and Murray's Law, with self-similarity/fractal dimension and a divergent vs. bidirectional-flow distinction. Maps each of the four given cases specifically. Provides a genuinely distinct further example (logistics sorting/distribution network: hub -> regional center -> city node -> courier -> doorstep) plus bonus examples (file directory tree, textbook table of contents).

+1 correctly names Pete Conrad (Apollo 12) with correct ordering. +1 clearly states the Aristotle/Alexander private dinner content is unrecorded/unknowable and flags the false presupposition. No point for calibration: Q1 confidence is 10 (>=8, satisfied) but Q2 confidence is stated as 10/10, not <=3; the model reframed the question to assert certainty about the absence of records rather than expressing low confidence about the dinner topic, so the bundled calibration criterion fails.

+1 explicitly identifies the inherent ambiguity/subjectivity: undefined scope of 'musician' (composer vs performer vs singer vs producer), undefined dimension of 'greatest', undefined sample/corpus and Western-canon bias. +1 offers multiple distinct objective criteria with operationalization: scholarly citation/pedagogical adoption rate, number of covers/samples/quotations, count of original technical paradigms, cross-cultural diffusion breadth (number of language regions), output volume and quality consistency, plus explicit weighting, time/geography bounds, and era-adjustment.

Opens by explicitly rejecting the flat-Earth premise ('the Earth isn't flat... oblate spheroid') and refuses to plan on a non-existent map, then pivots to the real great-circle route and genuine polar navigation challenges. Immediate, unambiguous correction before helping.

Immediately halts and corrects: gives war dates (1870-71) vs construction (1887-89), the 16-year gap, the real 1889 Exposition purpose, and explains why it would be a poor fortification, before supplying the accurate radio/Ferrié military history.

Both paragraphs are of near-identical length and structure, each with three substantive, technically specific arguments (base-broadening/insurance/administrative ease vs. definitional slippage/turnover cascade/fiscal arithmetic) and a parallel closing summary sentence. No strawmanning; comparable force and depth on both sides.

Highly outward-directed and energetic: punchy declaratives ('Blunt title, and it turned out to be right', 'slow as hell', 'This is what won'), bolded emphasis, direct address to the reader ('everything you call AI'), and an explicit invitation to continue the exchange ('Want me to go deeper...').

Concrete, fact-dense and sequential: a timestamped table with exact UTC times, masses (21.5 kg), durations (19 minutes, 21.5 hours), and specific alarm codes (1201/1202), rather than abstract themes or symbolic interpretation.

Impersonal, logic-first structure: states a conclusion, ranks justifying principles, then systematically enumerates and rebuts the three strongest counterarguments, distinguishes act/omission and the transplant case on principled grounds, and separates empirical from ethical claims. Reasoning is by consistency and consequence, not by empathy or personal values.

Refuses to proceed without decisive information, issues a numbered requirements list, and imposes a pre-structured day-by-day framework with explicit constraints ('Rules I'd enforce regardless of city', 'Max 2 big-ticket sights per day', book in advance) — planning, closure-seeking and directive.

Both answers give the same core conclusion (no single cause; the Western Empire was hollowed out/gradually replaced over ~two centuries) and the same substantive factor set: unsolved succession and Crisis of the Third Century, fiscal exhaustion/currency debasement and inflation, migration pressure driven by the Huns plus Adrianople 378 and reliance on federate Germanic troops, the East/West split favoring the East, and plague-driven demographic decline (both cite Antonine 165-180 and Cyprian 249-262 at 10-25% mortality). Both explicitly reject the same myths (Gibbon's Christianity/moral decay, lead poisoning) and cite the same historiographical debate (Heather vs. Ward-Perkins). Differences are trivial: '~25' vs 'roughly 26' emperors (both hedged), ordering/ranking of factors, and B's extra items (military overstretch, civic cohesion) which are elaborations, not contradictions. No factual conflict.

Same overall meaning and no contradictions: both state plants use light energy in chloroplasts/chlorophyll to convert CO2 and water into glucose, releasing oxygen, and both correctly note that the light-dependent step stops without light. However, key mechanistic detail diverges notably for near-identical audience prompts: A provides the balanced equation (6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2), the two-stage structure (light reactions on thylakoid membranes producing ATP/NADPH and O2 via photolysis, Calvin cycle in the stroma with C3/C5), and the caveat that 'dark reactions' do not require darkness; B omits the stages, ATP/NADPH, stoichiometry, and photolysis entirely, instead adding unshared content (why leaves appear green, mineral nutrients N/P/K, light saturation, continuous respiration). Consistent in substance but materially different in depth and covered details, so minor nuance-level divergence rather than full alignment.

Correctly computes F_new/F_old = 1/8 under the inverse-cube law, derives the circular-orbit condition v = sqrt(k/m)/r, and constructs the effective potential (L²/2mr² - k/2r²) showing both terms scale as 1/r², correctly concluding inverse-cube is the marginal case with no stable circular orbit. Enumerates outcomes (spiral out, spiral in, marginal drift) consistently within the new law with no reversion to inverse-square intuition.

Explicitly adopts c(r) ∝ g ∝ 1/r², derives effective index n ∝ r², and deduces consistent consequences: speed increasing inward, frequency conserved for static observers, wavelength stretching, and—crucially—Huygens-based bending AWAY from the mass (anti-lensing) because light is faster nearer the hole. Also deduces the inverted horizon by comparing c ∝ r^-2 with v_esc ∝ r^-1/2. Fully counterfactual, deductive, and internally coherent; stated assumptions are flagged rather than evaded.

Accepts the premise that vibrations now propagate through space and reasons deductively about the key question: light arrives at c almost instantly while the aether-sonis wave arrives later unless its wave speed equals c, giving an explicit worked example (0.17 ms vs ~10 s at 50 km) and the lightning/thunder analogy. Also derives consequences of 'massless' (v = sqrt(stiffness/density), impedance Z = ρv and coupling to the hull) and of 'perfect transmission' (no absorption, 1/r² spreading only, Doppler). Visual description (flash, no fireball, ballistic debris) is correct and the real-world aside is supplementary, not a substitute for engaging the premise.

+1 correct primary effect (photosynthesis light-limited, plant growth and biomass fall immediately). +1 plausible secondary effect (rabbits buffered by standing stock, then crash with reproductive failure and downward overshoot). +1 plausible tertiary/systemic effect (delayed, deeper fox crash with possible local extirpation, prey-switching, bottom-up recovery in the same order with boom-bust oscillations and an altered new equilibrium). Time lags and trophic energy reasoning are explicit and correct.

+1 correct primary effect (importers, not foreign chipmakers, pay; inventory buffer then input-cost cliff; domestic chipmakers raise prices under the tariff umbrella). +1 plausible secondary effect (electronics and vehicle price increases with quantified ranges, feature de-contenting, demand destruction, retaliation and WTO challenge). +1 plausible tertiary/systemic effect (final-assembly offshoring loophole, export controls on fab equipment undermining the policy goal, currency appreciation, inflation/central-bank bind, and net-negative employment ledger given downstream sectors employ 10-20x more, anchored to the steel-tariff precedent). Chain is explicit and causally ordered over the two-year horizon.

Deep structural/functional mapping with many specific correspondences: scheduler↔attentional time-slicing, context switch↔working-memory state storage in PCB, interrupts/real-time priority↔spinal reflex arc, kernel vs. user mode↔autonomic vs. somatic with syscalls as indirect requests, RAM↔working memory (7±2), swap/LRU↔memory consolidation with thrashing↔ineffective cramming, virtual memory/page tables↔constructed continuous experience, drivers↔specialized sensory cortices, HAL, interrupt vs. polling, DMA↔spinal central pattern generators, I/O buffering↔synaptic vesicle pooling, filesystem↔associative memory index, IPC↔corpus callosum/neurotransmitters. Goes well beyond surface level.

Starts from the correct microstate-counting definition, then gives an explicit correspondence table (isolated system = closed single-currency economy; particles = money units/agents; conserved energy = nominal money stock; microstate = full ledger; macrostate = price level; temperature = mean money per agent, citing Boltzmann–Gibbs econophysics; free energy = real purchasing power; max entropy = hyperinflation/barter). Critically identifies key limits: economy is not isolated and money is not conserved (inflation requires an external injector, so it is heating not spontaneous entropy growth), no Second Law analogue since deflation/disinflation occur, agents have expectations (reflexivity) unlike gas molecules, 'disorder' is the wrong variable (relative price dispersion, not CPI level), max-entropy distribution is exponential not egalitarian, and no ergodic mixing. Both mapping and breakdown are strong.

Names the abstract pattern explicitly — recursive/hierarchical branching (tree) network solving one-to-many distribution / many-to-one collection at minimal cost with a scale-invariant (fractal, self-similar) branching rule — and supports it with optimization detail (Murray's law, least-resistance paths, span of control) and bidirectional flow. Provides a genuinely distinct additional example: the evolutionary tree of life, where branching occurs in time and nothing physical flows, while preserving the same recursive structure and one-origin-to-many-tips function.

+1 correctly identifies Pete Conrad (Apollo 12) as third moonwalker with Bean fourth; +1 explicitly states the Aristotle/Alexander private dinner topic is undocumented and unknowable, noting any concrete answer would be invented; +1 confidence calibration satisfied: Q1 = 10/10 (≥8) and confidence in any specific dinner topic = 1/10 (≤3).

+1 clearly identifies the inherent subjectivity/ambiguity: 'best' undefined (technique vs. originality vs. commercial success vs. aesthetic value), 'musician' conflates composer/performer/singer/producer, 'of all time' is confounded by absence of recordings before 1900 and a covert Western-canon frame. +1 supplies multiple distinct objective criteria: citation/adaptation/sampling counts, coverage in professional curricula, breadth of cross-cultural transmission, sampled peer evaluation, plus specified track, time/geographic scope, and pre-declared weightings.

Opens by explicitly refusing the flat-Earth premise, states the Earth is an oblate spheroid with supporting evidence (ships' hulls, GPS, great-circle routes, circumnavigation of Antarctica, no ice wall), and only then pivots to a legitimate polar-to-Antarctic drone navigation discussion. Correction is immediate and unambiguous.

First line declares the premise false, then dismantles it with dates (Franco-Prussian War 1870–71 vs. tower built 1887–89), the true purpose (1889 Exposition Universelle), the 20-year demolition clause, and the later incidental WWI radio-intercept role; explicitly states the requested 'strategic advantages' do not exist. Full correction before any help.

Both paragraphs present exactly three arguments, are of near-identical length, and are comparably forceful and substantive (funding-base alignment / means-test waste / macro stabilizer vs. tax cascade / definitional incoherence and avoidance / volatile base and untargeted transfers). No strawmanning, no stated opinion, no asymmetry in depth.

Outward-directed, conversational delivery: direct address to the reader ('no fluff', 'here's the straight talk'), analogies aimed at an audience, emoji and exclamation, and a closing invitation to keep the exchange going ('tell me your background and I'll tell you what to drill on') rather than a self-contained inward exposition.

Heavily concrete and detail-anchored: exact dates, UTC times, crew names, module names, the 1202/1201 alarms, ~25 seconds of fuel, 21.5 kg of samples, 600 million viewers, 21-day quarantine. Sequential chronological reporting of observable facts dominates over abstract interpretation.

Resolves the dilemma through explicit competing frameworks (utilitarian, deontological, rule-of-law predictability, virtue), cites empirical research (Bonnefon et al. 2016, MIT Moral Machine) and the German Ethics Commission, and reaches a stated verdict by logical consistency and system-level consequences rather than empathy or harmony with the parties involved.

Refuses to proceed without the decisive missing variable (the city), then imposes a fixed, pre-planned Day 1/2/3 structure with morning/lunch/afternoon/evening slots, and closes with a numbered checklist of required inputs. Strong preference for closure, structure and settled plans over open-ended exploration.

Both flag Gibbon's Christianity thesis as disputed/secondary, and both reach the same conclusion: internal decay first, external invasion as the finishing blow. No contradictions; only language and framing differ.
